turns.text: Alright, so you think it was a falcon who rang the dinner bell? Let’s get back to our little parrot here. Imagine I’m a parrot named Crackerly, and my diet consists solely of crackers. Now, every time a bell rings, a person comes in and gives me a cracker. After a while, even without the bell, just hearing the sound of the door can make me start pecking at the air, expecting my cracker. It’s all about association—my body learns to connect the sound of the door (or bell) with getting fed. So remember, it’s the dog (or in our case, the parrot) learning to associate the stimulus (sound) with the reward (cracker), not a bird ringing a bell to get fed!
